AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Exercise induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) is a frustrating morbidity of asthma in children. Obesity has been associated with asthma and with more severe EIB in asthmatic children.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To quantify the effect of BMI on the risk of the occurrence of EIB in children with asthma.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Data were collected from six studies in which exercise challenge tests were performed according to international guidelines. We included 212 Children aged 7-18 years, with a pediatrician-diagnosed mild-to-moderate asthma.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A total of 103 of 212 children (49%) had a positive exercise challenge (fall of FEV1  ≥ 13%). The severity of EIB, as measured by the maximum fall in FEV1 , was significantly greater in overweight and obese children compared to normal weight children (respectively 23.9% vs 17.9%; P = 0.045). Asthmatic children with a BMI z-score around +1 had a 2.9-fold higher risk of the prevalence of EIB compared to children with a BMI z-score around the mean (OR 2.9; 95%CI: 1.3-6.1; P < 0.01). An increase in BMI z-score of 0.1 in boys led to a 1.4-fold increased risk of EIB (OR 1.4; 95%CI: 1.0-1.9; P = 0.03). A reduction in pre-exercise FEV1 was associated with a higher risk of EIB (last quartile six times higher risk compared to highest quartile (OR 6.1 [95%CI 2.5-14.5]).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: The severity of EIB is significantly greater in children with overweight and obesity compared to non-overweight asthmatic children. Furthermore, this study shows that the BMI-z-score, even with a normal weight, is strongly associated with the incidence of EIB in asthmatic boys.
